session.question: How many respondents were used for recycling in the 206 survey, and what did the extended VBN theory explain best?
session.answer:
The recycling survey used 206 respondents. The extended value-belief-norm (VBN) theory explained sustainable purchase behavior best, relative to household energy and water use, mobility, and recycling. (onel2023transformingconsumptionthe chunk 1)

For purchase behavior, the strongest explanatory pattern included biospheric values, ecological worldview, personal norms, behavioral intention, awareness of consequences, ascription of responsibility, and low egoistic values. (onel2023transformingconsumptionthe chunk 1)

session.context:
pqac-e0f0910e: The study used four separate survey samples for different sustainable behaviors: 281 for purchase, 265 for household energy and water use, 273 for mobility, and 206 for recycling. The paper reports that the extended value-belief-norm (VBN) theory provided the strongest explanation for sustainable purchase behavior, compared with household energy and water use, mobility, and recycling. For purchase, key predictors included biospheric values, ecological worldview, personal norms, behavioral intention, awareness of consequences, ascription of responsibility, and low egoistic values.
From Naz Onel. Transforming consumption: the role of values, beliefs, and norms in promoting four types of sustainable behavior. Journal of Consumer Behaviour, 2023. URL: https://doi.org/10.1002/cb.2212, doi:10.1002/cb.2212.

pqac-a4c77e79: The study used four separate SEMs on 1,025 respondents, including 206 respondents for recycling. It tested an extended value-belief-norm (VBN) theory across purchase, household energy and water use, mobility, and recycling behaviors. The abstract says the extended VBN theory provided the best explanation for sustainable purchase behavior, while similar patterns appeared for the other behaviors but with weaker model fit and lower explanatory power. For recycling, the model still applied but was not identified as the best-explained behavior. Key factors included biospheric values, ecological worldview, personal norms, behavioral intention, awareness of consequences, ascription of responsibility, and low egoistic values.
From Naz Onel. Transforming consumption: the role of values, beliefs, and norms in promoting four types of sustainable behavior. Journal of Consumer Behaviour, 2023. URL: https://doi.org/10.1002/cb.2212, doi:10.1002/cb.2212.

pqac-bc7a38a3: The excerpt states that the study tested an extended value-belief-norm (VBN) theory across four sustainable behavior domains using separate SEMs. It notes that the extended VBN theory provided the best explanation for sustainable purchase behavior compared with household energy and water use, mobility, and recycling. For the recycling survey specifically, the excerpt only says there were 206 respondents and that similar results were found, but the model fit and explanatory power were lower than for purchase. Therefore, the best-explained outcome was not recycling; it was sustainable purchase behavior.
From Naz Onel. Transforming consumption: the role of values, beliefs, and norms in promoting four types of sustainable behavior. Journal of Consumer Behaviour, 2023. URL: https://doi.org/10.1002/cb.2212, doi:10.1002/cb.2212.

pqac-b6c47604: The paper studies willingness to acquire circular apparel among Brazilian and Dutch consumers using the Value-Belief-Norm (VBN) theory. It reports that the VBN variables generally explain circular behavior in the apparel industry and that the model’s paths are supported. The results suggest VBN predicts willingness to consume circular apparel better in the Netherlands than in Brazil, possibly because Brazilians perceive the behavior as more effortful. Materialistic values were not an important predictor overall, though they had some positive influence for Dutch consumers. The excerpt does not mention 206 respondents or a recycled/extended VBN theory specifically.
From Giovana Monteiro Gomes, Natália Guimarães Moreira, Thijs Bouman, Aldo Roberto Ometto, and Ellen van der Werff. Towards circular economy for more sustainable apparel consumption: testing the value-belief-norm theory in brazil and in the netherlands. Sustainability, 2022. URL: https://doi.org/10.3390/su14020618, doi:10.3390/su14020618.

pqac-88a8e1e7: The excerpt describes a 2023 study that integrated value-belief-norm (VBN) theory with environmental awareness to explain Chinese university students’ environmentally sustainable behavior as tourists. It reports an empirical sample of 301 university students from eastern China. Findings show environmental awareness positively influences biospheric, altruistic, and egoistic values; biospheric value predicts the new ecological paradigm (NEP); and the NEP, awareness of consequence, and personal norms are important mediators. The study concludes that the extended VBN framework can explain students’ environmentally sustainable behavior in tourism and supports sustainable tourism promotion.
From Zhihui Wang, Liangzhen Nie, Eila Jeronen, Lihua Xu, and Meiai Chen. Understanding the environmentally sustainable behavior of chinese university students as tourists: an integrative framework. International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health, 2023. URL: https://doi.org/10.3390/ijerph20043317, doi:10.3390/ijerph20043317.

contexts.context: The excerpt describes a 2023 Sustainability paper on hybrid car purchase intentions using Sustainability Theory of Planned Behavior (STPB) integrated with UTAUT2. It reports 1048 valid respondents and finds that perceived economic concerns and perceived authority support were the strongest indirect factors affecting behavioral intention, followed by perceived environmental concern. All TPB domains were significant, while only performance expectancy, hedonic motivation, and price value were significant among UTAUT2 factors. The framework was proposed as useful for assessing eco-friendly or smart technology products and could be extended to other studies and countries.

contexts.context: The excerpt describes a 2024 European survey of radiographers’ perceptions and actions regarding environmental sustainability in radiology departments. It reports that over 70% of respondents said they turn off devices after use, and that waste recycling attention is high but mostly limited to paper, plastic, and glass. Contrast-agent recycling procedures were implemented by 13% of respondents. A majority (66%) reported either the absence or unawareness of sustainability procedures in their workplace. The study concludes that radiographers recognize the importance of greener radiology departments, but there are gaps in knowledge and implementation.
